coverage.target: A delivery standard governing when a unit is done, not a behaviour a person performs. Enforced at each unit's completion checkpoint rather than by a story.

A delivery standard governing when a unit is done, not a behaviour a person performs. US1.17 was drafted for it and withdrawn at review: its personas did not want it, its criteria were about a committed file, and one defined done-ness. Treated exactly as FR0.1. Enforced by the committed check file, which already treats a missing row as an incomplete unit.

functional-design — the invitation lens is a mechanism, and the stories assert the behaviour it must produce rather than the lens itself [Q5]. US1.10 (AC1.10.1, AC1.10.2) pin the reachability boundary the lens has to enforce.

domain-design — the address and display-name columns need a disposition per deleting actor and a retention class before storage. A schema and governance obligation rather than a user-visible behaviour; D6 asserts the dispositions.
nfr-requirements — a measured performance property of lens resolution, already verified at 500x the target scale. No user-visible behaviour to assert in a story.
nfr-design — a prohibition on cached summary tables and denormalised counts. An architectural constraint, not a behaviour.
nfr-design — no eager per-lens data at login. An architectural constraint.
A testing-cadence rule: acceptance transitions are written test-first because they are authorization decisions. It governs how US1.10 and US1.13 are built, not what they assert.

reverse.target: FR1.9a, FR1.4a, FR1.8a — title, narrative and three criteria amended. The prior story's premise, 'without anyone inviting me', is inverted by the acceptance model.
FR1.9h — AC1.3.2a and AC1.3.3a supersede criteria that promised no invitation is ever sent and that a seat's state is deliberately not shown on the roster.
FR11.1a — AC1.6.2a supersedes an unconditional revert-to-dormant on deletion, which silently cleared a decline.
FR1.9a, FR1.9d, FR1.9g, FR1.16 — the accept-or-decline decision, and the bounded pending view.
FR1.7a, FR1.7b, FR1.7c — account creation, which no prior story covered because no prior requirement permitted it.
FR1.7f, FR1.9a — signup on a number a teacher already added, with the lookup naming neither teacher nor batch.
FR1.9c, FR1.9c.1, FR1.9c.2 — reversibility by the person who declined, and by nobody else.
FR1.9f.1, FR1.9f.2, FR1.9f.3 — declining stops generation and voids what accrued, as an append-only reversal.
FR1.9e, FR1.9h — a seat nobody accepts, and the roster states that make a mistyped number visible.
FR1.7d, FR1.7e, FR1.7f — signup's own abuse ceilings, and the assertion that the OTP path stays byte-identical after signup exists.

FR2.12, FR1.9i — AC2.5.1a supersedes a criterion permitting removal only while dormant, which once dormant collapsed into pending forbade removing any seat a teacher creates, blocking the recovery path from a mistyped number.
Drafted for FR0.2 and withdrawn at review as a delivery standard rather than a user story, consistent with FR0.1's treatment. The obligation stands in the requirement and the committed check file.
